title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook page for what it means to work at Redwood: our values, ways of working, role definitions and ladders, promotion and performance processes, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and the set of core internal tools all Redwoods should know. It is intended for all employees and managers as a reference during hiring, onboarding, career conversations, and daily operations.

1) Redwood at a glance
- Mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- Values: customer-first engineering, ownership and reliability, clear communication, and continuous learning.
- Company size: ~150 people; cross-functional teams (engineering, product, research, go-to-market, people-ops, security).

2) Ways of working
- Work model: Remote-first with optional office hubs (San Francisco, New York, London). Teams set core hours when necessary for synchronous work; managers define team-level collaboration norms.
- Communication: Use Slack for day-to-day, Confluence for persistent docs, and weekly team updates for status. Always create a Confluence page for multi-step processes and policy changes.
- Meeting guidelines: Keep meetings agenda-driven, include clear owner and next steps, and prefer async updates when possible.

3) Roles and career ladders (overview)
- Purpose: Provide consistent expectations for scope, impact, and competencies across functions.
- Ladders covered here: Engineering (IC & Manager), Product, Design, Research, Customer Success, Sales, and People Ops. Full ladder documents linked in the related pages section.

Example: Engineering ladder (summary)
- IC-1 (New grad / entry): Contributes to clearly scoped tasks; requires mentoring for design and tradeoffs.
- IC-2 (Intermediate): Independently owns components, writes maintainable code, participates in design reviews.
- IC-3 (Senior): Leads large features, mentors peers, sets technical direction for medium-sized areas.
- IC-4 (Staff): Cross-team technical leadership, shapes architecture, and drives reliability and performance initiatives.
- IC-5 (Principal/Distinguished): Company-level influence, defines long-term technical strategy, and represents Redwood in external forums.

Engineering manager ladder (summary)
- EM-1 (Manager): Owns one team, hiring and performance, and drives delivery commitments.
- EM-2 (Senior Manager): Manages multiple teams or a broader area, owns cross-team initiatives.
- EM-3 (Director): Leads org-level strategy, budgets, and long-term roadmaps.

Promotion & performance process
- Cadence: Performance reviews are biannual (mid-year calibration + year-end). Promotions are recommended during reviews or as exceptions for out-of-cycle promotions.
- Evidence required for promotion packet: role profile mapping, 3+ peer/partner testimonials, a manager write-up with examples of impact, and a calibration note.
- Timeline: Manager prepares packet → Peer/partner reviews → People Ops reviews for leveling consistency → Calibration committee decision (2–4 weeks).
- Appeals: If a candidate disagrees with outcome, they may request a review with People Ops and their manager within 30 days.

4) Hiring and interview guide (high level)
- Sourcing & screen: Recruiter screens resume and role fit, schedules initial hiring manager screen.
- Interview loop: Typical loop includes: technical screen (where applicable), take-home or system-design, 3–4 onsite/virtual interviews covering execution, system design, collaboration, and bar-raising.
- Interview rubric: Use the standard rubric (technical competency, problem-solving, collaboration, ownership). Interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours.
- Offer process: Hiring manager + recruiter draft compensation; People Ops approves against bands and equity guidelines; recruiter sends offer letter with 3 business days to accept.
- Background & docs: All offers contingent on background verification and signed confidentiality agreement as required.

New hire onboarding overview (first 90 days)
- Day 0: Welcome email from People Ops, paperwork (benefits, tax forms), laptop & hardware shipping confirmation, and Slack/Okta access.
- Day 1–7: New hire orientation (company, People Ops, security), team welcome, kickoff meeting with manager, and 1:1 setup schedule.
- Week 1–4: Core training (codebase walk-through, product overview, security training), first small shipping task assigned.
- Month 1–3: Quarterly goals set, cross-functional introductions, and milestone check-ins (30/60/90 with manager).

New hire checklist (quick)
1. Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment.
2. Confirm hardware and VPN/Okta access.
3. Join #all-hands, team channel, and relevant working groups.
4. Complete mandatory security and compliance training in LMS.
5. Meet with buddy and set 30/60/90 goals.

5) Benefits & perks (summary)
- Compensation: Competitive salary bands with annual performance compensation reviews. People Ops publishes target bands for each role; managers should consult People Ops for offers near band edges.
- Equity: All full-time employees receive an equity grant on hire and periodic refreshes tied to performance and role changes. Equity plan documents are maintained by Finance & People Ops.
- Health & insurance: Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution; domestic and international options where available.
- Time off: Generous PTO policy, plus company-wide shutdowns and 10 paid sick days. Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies (see People Ops benefits page).
- Retirement & financial: 401(k) with employer match (US), tax-advantaged local options in other countries, and financial planning sessions offered quarterly.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual learning stipend, conference budget, and internal brown-bag speaker series.
- Hardware & remote work stipend: Standard MacBook provision (or equivalent) with an annual refresh policy; $1,000 work-from-home stipend for desk/chair/monitor.
- Wellness: EAP, mental health benefits, and team wellness credits.

6) Internal tools & access guide
- Core identity & access: Okta for SSO (Slack, Gmail, Confluence, GitHub, AWS). Request access via the IT access form linked in People Ops.
- Communication: Slack for day-to-day; channels to note: #all-hands, #announcements, #ops-alerts, and your team channel. Use: urgent/alerts in #ops-alerts; async work in team channels.
- Documentation: Confluence for persistent docs. Create pages under the appropriate space (team or product). Use the page template for runbooks and PRDs.
- Code & CI: GitHub (org: redwood-inference) with protected branches on main/master; CI via GitHub Actions. Follow commit message conventions and PR templates.
- Ticketing & planning: Jira for engineering and product work; use the team’s board and label conventions. PMs own backlog structure.
- HR & payroll: HRIS (Workday) for personal info, time off requests, and payroll. Benefit enrollments are managed through the HRIS portal.
- Security & VPN: Company VPN for accessing internal-only resources; MFA enforced. Report lost devices to security immediately.
- Monitoring & incidents: PagerDuty for SRE rotations and on-call alerts; dashboards in Datadog and Redwood Console for product telemetry.

Internal tools quick start (first week)
1. Okta: Set up MFA and enroll your primary device.
2. Slack: Join team channels, set your profile & working hours.
3. Confluence: Read the team handbook and create your 30/60/90 page.
4. GitHub: Confirm repo access and follow the onboarding PR template.
5. HRIS: Complete tax and benefits forms.

7) Manager & people-ops responsibilities
- Manager responsibilities: Set expectations and goals, run regular 1:1s, conduct onboarding in the first 90 days, provide career development guidance, and submit promotion packets when appropriate.
- People Ops responsibilities: Benefits administration, leveling guidance, interview process oversight, new-hire orientation, and escalation for compensation or policy exceptions.

8) Frequently asked questions
- "How do I request flexible work arrangements?" — Talk to your manager; formal requests go to People Ops at people-ops@redwood.example.
- "What is the promotion timeline?" — Promotions are discussed during the biannual review cycles; out-of-cycle promotions are possible for exceptional impact.
- "Who do I contact for payroll discrepancies?" — Contact payroll@redwood.example and People Ops.

9) Template & sample artifacts (links)
- 30/60/90 plan template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/30-60-90
- Manager onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/manager-onboarding
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/promotion-packet

10) Ownership & change process
- Document owner: People Ops (Ava Martinez).
- Review cadence: Annual review or sooner when policies change (e.g., benefits, legal/regulatory changes).
- How to propose changes: Open a pull request on the Confluence page (or email people-ops@redwood.example) with rationale, impacts, and proposed text.

Appendix: Contacts & escalation
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood.example
- Payroll & benefits: payroll@redwood.example
- IT & hardware: it-support@redwood.example
- Security incidents: security@redwood.example (for data-loss or compromised credentials)
- Emergency on-call (SRE): see PagerDuty rotation in Confluence
